name: Vitamin D
summary: Fix a deficiency, don't chase a boost. Correcting low vitamin D can help muscle strength (especially lower-body) and general health; supplementing when you're already replete does little for performance.
effect: In deficient or insufficient athletes, supplementation improves lower-limb strength; little-to-no effect on upper-limb strength or explosive power, and no clear ergogenic benefit once levels are already adequate.
dosing: Typically 1000-2000 IU/day to reach and maintain sufficiency; if you suspect deficiency, test 25(OH)D and dose to your level with a clinician. More is not better.
timing: Irrelevant to timing; take with a fat-containing meal for absorption.
safety: Safe at typical doses; chronic megadoses risk toxicity (hypercalcemia). Test and dose sensibly rather than guessing high.
